answer: A stake-bonded reputation voyage works like this: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and its standing grows only through a slow delta of verified work over weeks, not instant volume. A haven of trusted attestors vouches for behavior, but one bad attestation slashes the voucher's own stake too. An attacker cloning a thousand identities must fund a thousand deposits and wait out the same slow ramp, so faking reputation costs more than the clones could ever extract.
